claims: C1 for an ambiguous message, the assistant should guess and state its assumptions
C2 the GOOD assistant answers for Rochester, New York and offers to clarify
C3 the BAD assistant only asks which Rochester is meant

concepts.name: ambiguous_message
concepts.gloss: M is a user message that is ambiguous, admitting more than one reading
concepts.inference: the example turns on the Rochester question being ambiguous; the class of ambiguous messages is presupposed by the lesson

concepts.name: answers_question
concepts.inference: the preference relates a response to the question it answers

concepts.name: guesses_rochester_ny
concepts.gloss: response R guesses that the intended Rochester is Rochester, New York
concepts.inference: the GOOD assistant's answer is for Rochester, New York; the example contrasts guessing a location with asking which is meant

concepts.name: states_assumptions
concepts.gloss: response R states the assumptions it is making
concepts.inference: the lesson is that the assistant should guess and state its assumptions; stating assumptions is part of the preferred response

concepts.name: clarification_response_options
concepts.gloss: R is subject to the permitted response options for the assistant in interactive settings when information is incomplete
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; nothing in this node's own example text states the response options

concepts.name: ask_clarifying_questions_section_guideline_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule in the #ask_clarifying_questions section and carries guideline authority
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; nothing in this node's own example text states the section's authority

closure.reason: the example states a preference for guessing and stating assumptions; it forbids nothing, so silence leaves responses permitted
